english: Cohort Tracking
Following the same children across rounds, and who does what with the data.
Cohort tracking
Cohort tracking follows the same groups of children over time.
In SARMAAN II, cohort tracking follows groups of children who receive AZM in each round. Their health outcomes are monitored over time.
Keeping eligible children in the programme for the whole campaign is a key challenge.
Retention tracking shows the programme's effectiveness.
Cohort tracking monitors each enrolled child across many treatment rounds.
The DIGIT HCM app lets data managers track the same children over successive rounds.
Why cohort tracking
Measure effectiveness: see how well AZM reduces under-5 illness and death.
Monitor safety: find side effects or adverse reactions.
Evaluate coverage and adherence: check children receive every round.
Policy decisions: guide governments and partners to expand, adjust or improve AZM campaigns.
Who is responsible
CDDs give AZM and record the children treated in DIGIT HCM.
Supervisors ensure data is collected correctly and cohorts are defined.
M&E teams analyse cohort data, track drop-out and give timely feedback.
Government and IPs use the findings to adjust campaign strategies.
Step — data moves from CDDs to supervisors, to M&E teams, to government and partners.
Cohort tracking responsibility flow (transcribed from image)
Community Drug Distributors: administer treatment; collect data (field work).
CDD Supervisors, Health Facility Supervisors, Nat'l, State and LGA Team: monitor and verify data (supervision).
State and Country M&E Team: analyze and compare cohorts (data analysis).
Government and Partners: policy decisions; program adjustments (policy action).
